q: Singular perturbation problems (fast-slow systems) with ẋ = f(x,y), εẏ = g(x,y) (ε → 0) are analysed by Fenichel's geometric singular perturbation theory. The slow manifold is:
opts: An O(ε) perturbation of the critical manifold {g(x,y) = 0} that is invariant for small ε > 0
The set where both f = 0 and g = 0
An invariant torus for the fast system
exp: Fenichel's theorem: near a normally hyperbolic compact piece of the critical manifold S₀ = {g = 0}, there exists a slow invariant manifold S_ε = S₀ + O(ε) on which dynamics reduces to a slower system. This formalises Tikhonov's theorem geometrically.
